name: a_macro_secondary
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Secondary macro & officials.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Regional Fed surveys (Dallas, Richmond, Kansas City, Empire, Philly) actual vs prior; every Fed governor/president speech with verbatim quotes; Treasury and White House economic appointments; fiscal watchdog reports (CBO, CRFB) on debt and rates; foreign CEOs of US-listed companies commenting on trade/export controls.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Fed Officials [Macro]

- Federal Reserve Vice Chair **Philip Jefferson** said future policy adjustments should depend on “incoming data, the evolving outlook and the balance of risks”; he said policymakers’ judgment “may take more time” and described the economy as facing a “cascade of shocks” from energy prices, AI infrastructure investment and trade-policy changes. The remarks were delivered Thursday and reported Friday, October 2. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, 08:23 ET)[2]

- New York Fed President **John Williams** said there was “no need for urgency” in changing monetary policy and that the Fed had “time to gather more information”; he also said “one further upward adjustment” could be appropriate later in 2026. (CNBC TV18, Oct. 2, publication time not provided)[8]

- Chicago Fed President **Austan Goolsbee** said there was “plenty of room for anything to be on the table” when asked whether the Fed should raise rates or pause at its next meeting. (Reuters, Oct. 2, publication time not provided)[12]

- Dallas Fed President **Lorie Logan** said the federal-funds target range needed to rise by “an additional 50 basis points or more” to balance risks and the Fed’s dual-mandate goals. Her remarks were delivered Thursday and reported during the October 2 window. (Bloomberg, Oct. 2, publication time not provided)[4]

- Minneapolis Fed President **Neel Kashkari** said, “I don’t have a strong view” on whether the next rate increase should occur at the end of October; he said his forecast called for one more rate hike in 2026 and another in 2027. His comments were made Thursday and reported during the window. (CNBC TV18, Oct. 2, publication time not provided)[8]

- Richmond Fed President **Tom Barkin**, Boston Fed President **Susan Collins** and Kansas City Fed President **Jeff Schmid** declined to state their expected policy paths for the Fed’s final two meetings of 2026 at an Asheville, North Carolina conference. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 2, publication time not provided)[3]

- Traders priced approximately a **25% probability** of an October rate increase, down from approximately **70%** earlier in the week, according to federal-funds futures pricing cited in reports published October 2. (CNBC TV18, Oct. 2, publication time not provided)[8]

## Federal Reserve [Macro / Calendar]

- The Federal Reserve Board extended the comment period for its proposal to modernize **Regulation O** until **November 4, 2026**; comments had originally been due October 5. (Federal Reserve, Oct. 2, 16:02 ET)[7]

## Fiscal and Economic Policy [Macro]

- The available search results did not provide a qualifying CBO or Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget report published between October 2, 2026 and October 5, 2026 at 12:20 ET concerning federal debt or interest rates.

## Regional Fed Surveys [Macro / Calendar]

- The available search results did not provide qualifying October 2–5, 2026 releases for the **Dallas, Richmond, Kansas City, Empire State or Philadelphia Fed surveys** with actual-versus-prior figures.

## Treasury and White House Appointments [Macro / Calendar]

- The available search results did not provide a qualifying Treasury or White House economic appointment announcement published between October 2, 2026 and October 5, 2026 at 12:20 ET.

## Foreign CEOs and Trade Controls [Geopolitics / Semiconductors]

- The available search results did not provide a qualifying report published between October 2, 2026 and October 5, 2026 at 12:20 ET in which a foreign CEO of a US-listed company commented on trade restrictions or export controls.
